name: Channels, terminal and package as ways in
description: Each way in is its own measured solution, and every one hands its request to the same router. The package's front door is taught by its documents (explain-qar), shown by its examples (learn-by-example) and set up through one layered configuration (configure-a-lane).
advantages: A new channel is one more solution beneath this one, measured on its own.
disadvantages: No metric judges the ways in together; only each one's own.

name: In-memory thread-safe inbox
description: Holds a dictionary of per-conversation lists behind a lock inside the library's inbox module, satisfying the port with push, drain and peek. The orchestrator drains it between planner steps. Measured by plugging it into the live orchestrator and running synthetic cases where messages are pushed before or during a run, plus direct port-contract operations, with no model calls.
advantages: Simple, fast, thread-safe, and app-agnostic, so the same inbox serves chat, a frontend or anything else; the measurement checks delivery through the real planning loop and catches loss or cross-conversation leaks. Selected because: fixed in code
disadvantages: State is lost on restart and is not shared across processes or hosts, so a multi-process deployment needs a different implementation; the cases do not cover the deep retry boundary where a subprocess cannot be re-prompted.

name: One vision-model call per image (today)
description: Each attached image is sent to the configured vision model with a describe prompt and the text is added to the grounding.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: No description, the image is named only (proposed)
description: Proposed. The image is listed by name and type with no description, so no vision call is made.
advantages: No cost; no image data leaves the process.
disadvantages: The reply cannot use what is in the image; not built.
